name: Henri Li
body: Henry Li is a Research Software Engineer at San Diego State University's Cyberinfrastructure and Research IT department. He completed his Master's in Computer Science at the University of California San Diego (UCSD). He often collaborates with researchers from UCSD and SDSU. His work currently includes enabling access for researchers across the California State University system through the NSF-funded Technology Infrastructure for Data Exploration (TIDE) program and for researchers across the United States through the National Artificial Intelligence Research Resource (NAIRR) Pilot. Previously he has worked as a technology consultant for cloud computing at IBM and at PriceWaterhouseCoopers before attending his master's program.

name: Victoria Nguyen
body: Victoria Nguyen graduated from UC San Diego in 2021 with a Bachelors in Applied Mathematics and Management Science. She interned at the San Diego Supercomputer Center and following her graduation, she acquired a full-time position there. She currently supporting the Research Data Services (RDS) division and the CAIDA research group as a Systems Integration Engineer and System Admin respectively.

name: Hovakim Grabski
description: Hovakim Grabski is a visiting scholar from Armenia and Researcher/SysAdmin at Abagyan Lab, UC San Diego and SDSC, with experience in Python programming, ICM programming language for molecular modeling, docking, screening, and infrastructure automation.
body:
Hovakim Grabski is a visiting scholar from Armenia and Researcher/SysAdmin at Abagyan Lab, UC San Diego and SDSC, with experience in Python programming, ICM programming language for molecular modeling, docking, screening, and infrastructure automation. His work involves backend development, containerization, and high-performance computing (HPC) using platforms like SLURM and HashiCorp Nomad. Hovakim has worked on designing and managing pipelines for virtual screening of chemical compounds, utilizing GPUs to optimize scientific workflows. He has been working in Linux environments for over a decade, with experience across various distributions including Ubuntu and AlmaLinux.

His research background includes molecular dynamics simulations, database deployment, and microservice architecture. He has been involved in data science and big data analytics, contributing to projects in computational biology and chemistry. Hovakim has been fortunate to receive a few fellowships and awards, such as the Cyberinfrastructure Fellowship from SDSC and participating in Google Summer of Code. He is focused on continuous learning and enjoys solving problems in his field.
